transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's so nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... I guess what brings me in is... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I've just been having this sort of restless feeling? It's probably not a huge deal, I know everyone gets a little antsy sometimes, but it's like I'm wound just a little too tight, and I can't seem to fully settle down. 

Even when I'm doing things where I'm supposed to be, you know, perfectly calm—like sitting through a long planning meeting for work, or even when I'm just trying to relax by painting or doing yoga. I just can't quite get my body to be still and relax. Does that make sense? I feel a little silly even bringing it up, to be honest, but I just wanted to see if maybe that's something you could help with?
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized or revved up compared with your normal self?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. Not compared to my normal self, anyway. I mean, I always have that sort of baseline hum of being a little restless, like I mentioned, but it doesn't really spike into anything extreme. 

It's not like I suddenly get these huge bursts of energy out of nowhere where I'm acting out of character or anything like that. I'm just naturally a bit of a busy bee, I guess? Working in wholesale buying, you kind of have to stay on your toes, so I always just tried to channel it into being productive. But no, nothing unusual or where I feel out of control. 

Is... is that what you meant by revved up? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Do these restless feelings ever come on as sudden attacks of intense fear or panic?

Oh, goodness, no. Nothing like that at all. I don't get panic attacks or anything scary like that. 

It's really just a mild, physical fidgetiness. Like my foot wants to tap, or I just need to shift around in my chair. It's never accompanied by fear or panic or feeling like something terrible is going to happen. I'm actually a very positive person most of the time! 

I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. It's just a little annoying, you know? Not terrifying at all. Does that help clear it up?
Did this restless feeling begin after you started or changed any medication?

Oh, um, no, no medication changes. I'm actually not taking anything right now, just my usual daily vitamins. I try to stay pretty healthy, you know? 

So, no, it's definitely not a side effect of a pill or anything like that. It's just... well, just me, I suppose. I hope that's okay? I mean, I know it would probably be easier to figure out if it was just a medication issue, but... yeah, no new meds.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to worry?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I have normal, everyday things I think about, like keeping track of inventory or making sure orders are right for work, but... well, I definitely don't just sit around worrying for no reason. 

I try to keep a really positive outlook on life! I'd hate for you to think I'm a naturally anxious or pessimistic person, because I'm really not. I usually just try to take things in stride and stay upbeat. It's really just that physical fidgety feeling I mentioned before, not a worried mind, if that makes sense? 

I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information. Does that answer what you were asking?
Since childhood, have you usually had trouble sitting still?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose so. I was just a very, very enthusiastic kid, you know? 

I do remember back in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes send notes home to my parents. It wasn't because I was a bad kid or anything! I just... well, I kept popping out of my seat a lot. And I guess I had a bit of a habit of talking over my classmates, or I'd rush to blurt out an answer before the teacher even finished asking the question. 

I just got so excited about participating, and I had all this energy. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a terror in the classroom, because I always meant well, I promise! I just had a hard time keeping it all contained. Does that sound like the kind of thing you're asking about?
